c.tagline: Home of the blues, the birthplace of rock 'n' roll, and the soul of Southern barbecue.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around $2.50 plus per-mile charges; app-based Uber and Lyft are widely used and usually cheaper than hailing a cab.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance; 311 is Memphis's non-emergency city line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

solo.f: fine in tourist areas; night caution

avoid.reason: Elevated violent crime; caution beyond downtown/Beale St; several neighborhoods high-crime

hood_desc: The walkable core along the Mississippi riverfront, home to the neon-lit Beale Street blues clubs, the National Civil Rights Museum at the Lorraine Motel, and the Peabody ducks; the best base for first-timers who want music, history, and nightlife on foot.

A revitalized district of art galleries, indie boutiques, and buzzy restaurants south of Beale, anchored by the historic Central Station and the Arcade Restaurant; suits younger travelers wanting a creative, trolley-connected scene.

Memphis's leafy entertainment and arts heart, with the Overton Square theater and dining district, Overton Park, the Memphis Brooks Museum, and the zoo; a lively yet local base with bars, patios, and cafes.

A bohemian, tree-lined neighborhood famous for its restaurant-and-bar cluster around the Cooper-Young intersection, murals, and vintage shops; suits travelers wanting an offbeat, foodie, community feel.

The residential south-side district built around Graceland, Elvis Presley's mansion and estate; convenient to the airport and the ultimate base for Elvis pilgrims, though quieter and more spread out than the core.

water.note: Tap water from the artesian Memphis Sand aquifer is safe and locally celebrated.

transit.hours: MATA buses run roughly 4:30am to midnight depending on route; the vintage Main Street Trolley runs from mid-morning to around 10-11pm, later on weekends.
transit.note: Memphis is largely car-dependent; the restored vintage Main Street Trolley is handy for getting around Downtown and the riverfront, but reaching Midtown, Graceland, or East Memphis usually needs a car or ride-hail.
transit.pay: Pay cash on board (exact fare) or use a reloadable MATA fare card or the MATA transit app. A single bus or trolley ride is $1.75, a vintage Main Street Trolley ride is $1, and a day pass is about $3.50.

train: Memphis Central Station (Amtrak City of New Orleans)

transit.m: MATA Route 2 bus toward Downtown (~45-60 min)

tip.r: ~18-20% at restaurants; $1-2 per drink at bars and ~15% for taxi rides.
